messages:
ops_incident_bot: ALERT triggered: KV_CACHE_CONTINUOUS_BATCH_HIGH_ERROR rate > 5% across region-us-east-1 (2632109876) :rotating_light:
ops_incident_bot: Symptoms: sustained latency spikes (p95 > 900ms), increased 500s from runtime, and rapid growth of prefix-key space. Paging on-call.

laura: on call, looking now. I'm seeing the alert dashboard — can anyone confirm recent deploys to runtime or model catalog?

ashwin: we rolled model v2.14.0 to hosted catalog ~10m before the alert. there was a tokenizer tweak (preserve_special_tokens=true) in that rollout. Might affect prefix hashing.

sam: running quick grep on runtime logs, lots of TTL:0 evictions and "KVKeyLengthExceeded" traces. paste:```
[2026-03-15T12:01:05Z] warn runtime: prefix_cache: key_count=12.3M, avg_key_len=128, miss_rate=0.72
[2026-03-15T12:01:06Z] error runtime: continuous_batch: failed to allocate batch: alloc_err=kv_quota_exceeded
[2026-03-15T12:01:07Z] error runtime: tokenizer: canonicalize(): token mismatch for template_id=prompt-891
```

sam: looks like many cached prefix keys are no longer matching incoming prompt hashes -> cache blowup + higher batching overhead -> latency cliff.

marie: customer impact estimate? any targeted tenants?

sam: initial filter: 5% of requests across all hosted API keys, but concentrated on a handful of high-throughput customers (IDs: cust-17, cust-48, cust-99). Some 502s observed when batch paths fail.

laura: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle continuous batching to fall back to single-request mode, 2) pin model to previous version for hosted traffic, 3) scheduled cache scrub of invalid prefixes with TTL ramp-down. Who can execute 1 & 2 now?

oncall-sre: I can flip throttle. will set continuous_batch.max_inflight=0.1 (10% of normal) and max_concurrent_batches=1 for region-us-east-1 to limit pressure. applying now.

oncall-sre: command run:```bash
curl -X POST "$RUNTIME_API/ops/configs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"scope":"us-east-1","continuous_batch":{"max_inflight":0.1,"max_concurrent_batches":1}}'
```
noncall-sre: change is live, saw immediate p95 drop from 920ms -> 360ms in ~30s.

ashwin: I'll revert the model rollout for hosted catalog to v2.13.7 across the affected region. executing canary rollback now.

ashwin: rollback command:```
./catalogctl promote --model-id redwood/v2.13.7 --region us-east-1 --force --reason "tokenizer-induced key drift"
```

ashwin: rollback started. note: we still need to address stale keys in KV store — they won't be compatible with prior tokenizer if they were created by the new tokenizer. recommending a staged scrub that sets TTLs rather than mass delete.

sam: agree — mass delete will cause a siege of cache misses and a second spike. Suggested approach: set a short TTL (e.g., 300s) on keys that look like they were generated post-rollout, then observe. We can detect post-rollout keys by hashing fingerprint header present in stored metadata (e.g., tokenizer_fingerprint=0x7a5b).

sam: sample redis command to set TTL pattern (run on shard leader):```bash
redis-cli -h kv-shard-12 --scan --pattern "prefix:*:tf:7a5b*" | xargs -L100 redis-cli -h kv-shard-12 EXPIRE 300
```

marie: can we get a short customer-facing blurb for impacted customers? SRE required it for support.

laura: draft: "We observed increased latency and intermittent errors on the Redwood hosted API affecting a subset of high-throughput customers. We have throttled batch processing and are rolling back a recent model catalog change while we safely clean affected cache entries. No data loss is expected; updates will follow as we confirm stability. — Redwood Inference Ops"

miguel: I can take over the live handoff in 30m. laura — please add runbook and current state in the incident doc and drop handoff note here.

laura: handoff notes: 1) continuous_batch throttled (max_inflight=0.1) at 12:03Z, 2) rollback to v2.13.7 initiated at 12:04Z, 3) identified tokenizer_fingerprint=0x7a5b as suspect, 4) plan to EXPIRE post-rollout keys with TTL 300s, 5) customer impact ~5% requests (cust-17/cust-48/cust-99) experiencing p95 ~900ms -> stabilized to ~360ms.

ops_incident_bot: INCIDENT KV-BATCH-2663 assigned to oncall-sre and ml-infra; priority P1. Pager duty: page-schedule-ops triggered.

miguel: Ack, taking lead. next immediate actions I'll coordinate: a) finish rollback verification, b) run key TTL sweep progressively across shards, c) monitor for re-spike for 15m windows, d) prepare postmortem skeleton.

ashwin: one thing to add — we should record which prompt templates used the new canonicalization. sample python snippet to find tokens that changed between tokenizers:```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
old = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer_v2.13.7.json')
new = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer_v2.14.0.json')
for t in ["@user","\\n","<sep>"]:
    print(t, old.encode(t).ids, new.encode(t).ids)
```

sam: noted. I'll also add a runtime guard to detect unseen tokenizer_fingerprint values in the header and route them to a soft-path (no caching) for a short burn-in period in the future. Quick patch queued: runtime hardening PR #4021.

marie: SRE/Support — please create support tickets for cust-17/48/99 with the draft message and mark as "incident: KV-BATCH-2663".

laura: created support tickets and pinged account reps.

miguel: TTL sweep started shard 1-4. running command with safe concurrency. progress updates: shard1 done (12:18Z, ~4k keys expired), shard2 running.

sam: monitoring dashboard shows error-rate down to 1.2% and p95 at 320ms post-throttle + rollback. still watching.

oncall-sre: rolling back continuous_batch throttle to 0.2 after TTL ramp shows positive trend, will keep conservative config until TTLs expire.

miguel: note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = tokenizer change produced incompatible canonicalized prompt hashes which bypassed prefix cache hit path, causing large influx of distinct keys and breakdown of batching heuristics. Contributing factors: insufficient rollout canary for tokenization changes, no tokenizer_fingerprint soft-path, no automated prefix-key TTL on model changes.

laura: action items assigned: 
- ashwin: add tokenizer_fingerprint to model rollout checklist + add model rollback automations (ETA: 48h)
- sam: runtime soft-path for unknown fingerprint + PR #4021 (ETA: 24h)
- miguel: incident postmortem draft + customer notes (ETA: EOD)
- oncall-sre: default batch throttle guards in runtime config (ETA: 12h)

miguel: handing off to oncall-sre for monitoring overnight. I'll post postmortem link once skeleton done. thanks all. :heart:

ops_incident_bot: INCIDENT KV-BATCH-2663 status: mitigated -> monitoring. next update expected 2026-03-15T20:00Z or sooner if regression.
